title: HeaderForm derives Hash but HeaderValueTyped does not — asymmetric, blocks valid use cases
description: header_typed.rs:130 `HeaderForm` derives `Hash`. header_typed.rs:152 `HeaderValueTyped` does not. Every payload variant's type is `Hash`-able (`String`, `Vec<EmailAddress>`, `Vec<AddressGroup>`, `Vec<String>`, `Option<HeaderDateTime>`) provided the inner structs also derive `Hash` (see related missing-Hash issues on EmailAddress/AddressGroup/HeaderDateTime). A JMAP server caching by `(form, raw_bytes)` or deduping (form, result) pairs cannot use `HashSet<HeaderValueTyped>` or `HashMap<HeaderValueTyped, T>`. The asymmetry (selector hashable, result not) is the kind of API gap a serious Rust practitioner notices on first reading. Derive `Hash` on all the public payload types and on `HeaderValueTyped` itself.
close_reason: Type-definition cleanup batch on the typed header surface: (.4) added #[non_exhaustive] to EmailAddress and AddressGroup (HeaderDateTime was already done); (.5) dropped Copy from HeaderDateTime; (.26) dropped Copy from HeaderForm; (.18/.19/.20) added Display impls — RFC 5322 §3.4 mailbox/group form for EmailAddress/AddressGroup, RFC 3339 form for HeaderDateTime; (.34/.35) added Hash on EmailAddress/AddressGroup/HeaderDateTime/HeaderValueTyped; (.36) added Default on EmailAddress/AddressGroup; (.33) symmetric by-value internal signature on to_mail_parser/from_mail_parser. New public constructors EmailAddress::new and AddressGroup::new for callers blocked by #[non_exhaustive]. New tests cover Display, Hash, and TzSign.
